title: About the North Carolina Project Portal

aims.text:
The North Carolina Office of State Budget & Management (OSBM) develops, launches, and enhances partnerships between state government and North Carolina's research and philanthropic sectors. This includes elevating the State's internal capacity to use and generate evidence in its policy and programmatic functions.

Tthe NC Project Portal facilitates this work by sharing state agency research needs and empowering people with a way to express interest in partnering to work on those needs.

If you're interested in working on a project, please connect. State agencies seeks partners from a wide range of disciplines. Project summaries include information about what types of expertise are likely needed, but if you have a different idea for how to contribute, just let us know.

After OSBM collects expressions of interest, the potential partners work together to assess the best approach the project and partnership fit. OSBM prioritizes partnerships that are scalable, sustainable, and develop public, open-source resources.

To learn more about how OSBM supports operational excellence across the state, see [OSBM's Operational Excellence portfolio](https://www.osbm.nc.gov/operational-excellence).

faq.title: Do I need to have prior experience working with government?
faq.text: Nope. We hope that the NC Project Portal encourages people who have not worked with government to consider doing so.

faq.title: Are these opportunities open to students?
faq.text: Yes, for some projects. Express your interest even if you're unsure whether your expertise is a good fit. The needs of the agency along with research partner input, determine what type of expertise will fit best for each project.

faq.title: Can multiple people or organizations work on a project?
faq.text: Yes. Needs vary from project to project with respect to scope, expertise needed, timeline, and other factors. If you are interested in working with one or more collaborators but have not identified them, contact [partnerships@osbm.nc.gov] (mailto:partnerships@osbm.nc.gov).

faq.title: Is there funding for projects?
faq.text: It depends. Agencies and research partners work together to determine if a project has costs, what funding may be available, and possibilities for pursuing funding. OSBM works with a number of funders who are interested in supporting applied research in the state, if the methods are rigorous and the learnings are tailored to inform [Priority Questions](https://www.osbm.nc.gov/operational-excellence/priority-questions-and-learning-agendas).

faq.title: What kind of data are available?
faq.text: It depends. Agency and research partners work together to assess what data would advance a project and, in turn, whether and how to collect and share it. There are a wide variety of data already collected for research or administrative purposes, which may be leveraged for a project; or new data collection may be needed.

faq.title: Can I propose a project idea?
faq.text: Absolutely! Please email [partnerships@osbm.nc.gov](mailto:partnerships@osbm.nc.gov) with a brief description of your proposed project: the basic idea, how results would benefit North Carolinians, what you're seeking in a parter, and an estimated timeline. "Brief" means a few bullets by email, or an attached 1-pager; if the concept seems like a potential fit, we'll schedule a meeting to discuss and get into more details.
